Inspected the published supplier def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding, its Definition section. Exact supplier excerpt: “An exact dyadic rational is a number $m2^q$ with integers $m,q$.
Fix integers $p\ge2$ and $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$. Put
$\eta=2^{e_{\min}-p+1}$ and
$N_{\max}=(2^p-1)2^{e_{\max}-p+1}$. The finite representable set $\mathbb F$
consists of zero, both signs of every normal number $k2^{e-p+1}$ with integers $e,k$ satisfying
$e_{\min}\le e\le e_{\max}$ and $2^{p-1}\le k<2^p$, and both signs of every
subnormal number $k\eta$ with integer $k$ satisfying $1\le k<2^{p-1}$. The smallest positive
subnormal is $\eta$, the smallest positive normal is $2^{e_{\min}}$, and the
largest finite magnitude is $N_{\max}$. The extended endpoint set also contains
$-\infty$ and $+\infty$ as enclosure sentinels; they are not finite machine
numbers.”. Consumer use: Use [[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]]: each finite. The supplied hypotheses, determinant/rounding conventions and claim direction match this use. This records author inspection, not independent approval.

Inspected the published supplier def-intervals-rectangles-and-complex-balls, its Definition section. Exact supplier excerpt: “A **real interval** is a closed set $[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ with finite dyadic
endpoints $a\le b$. Its width is $b-a$, midpoint is $(a+b)/2$, and its
midpoint-radius form is $m+[-r,r]$ with $m=(a+b)/2$ and $r=(b-a)/2$. The empty
set is the status `empty`; the whole real line is `entire`. `overflow`,
`domain-error`, `split-domain`, and `inconclusive` are computation statuses,
not finite intervals.”. Consumer use: as defined in [[def-intervals-rectangles-and-complex-balls]]. Its values remain. The supplied hypotheses, determinant/rounding conventions and claim direction match this use. This records author inspection, not independent approval.

Inspected the published supplier def-complete-ordered-real-field, its Definition section. Exact supplier excerpt: “A **Dedekind-complete ordered field** is a commutative field $\mathbb R$ with
identity $1>0$, a total order compatible with addition and multiplication, and
the least-upper-bound axiom: every nonempty subset of $\mathbb R$ that is
bounded above has a least upper bound in $\mathbb R$. Throughout this batch,
all real variables, intervals, limits, derivatives and integrals are taken in
such a field. The integers and rationals are interpreted in their usual
embedded copies. For $x\in\mathbb R$, define $|x|=x$ when $x\ge0$ and
$|x|=-x$ when $x<0$.”. Consumer use: comparisons use the order of [[def-complete-ordered-real-field]]. For a positive. The supplied hypotheses, determinant/rounding conventions and claim direction match this use. This records author inspection, not independent approval.

Inspected the published supplier def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations, its Definition section. Exact supplier excerpt: “For real intervals $X=[a,b]$ and $Y=[c,d]$, compute the displayed exact
endpoint formulas and round the lower endpoint down and the upper endpoint up
in the format of
[[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]]. If either exact
endpoint overflows, return `overflow` with the outward extended endpoints;
never substitute a finite endpoint for an overflow sentinel. Addition is
$[a+c,b+d]$, subtraction is $[a-d,b-c]$, and multiplication is
$[\min(ac,ad,bc,bd),\max(ac,ad,bc,bd)]$. Division is defined only when
$0\notin Y$ and is $X[1/d,1/c]$, with reciprocal endpoints computed as exact
rationals before outward rounding. Squaring is
$[0,\max(a^2,b^2)]$ when $0\in X$ and
$[\min(a^2,b^2),\max(a^2,b^2)]$ otherwise. Square root is defined only for
$X\subseteq[0,\infty)$ and is enclosed by applying
[[alg-dyadic-square-root-bisection]] to the exact dyadic endpoints with
request $n=p$, where $p$ is the selected format precision, and rounding
outward for storage.”. Consumer use: [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]. If every operation. The supplied hypotheses, determinant/rounding conventions and claim direction match this use. This records author inspection, not independent approval.

Inspected the published supplier thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound, its Statement section and complete proof. Exact supplier excerpt: “For real intervals, complex rectangles or complex balls on which an operation
is defined, enlarging either input enclosure cannot shrink the computed
enclosure: for binary $\circ\in\{+,-,\times,\div\}$, if $X\subseteq X'$ and
$Y\subseteq Y'$, then the computed set enclosure of $X\circ Y$ is contained
in that of $X'\circ Y'$ whenever both are finite results and their domain
restrictions are preserved. The square-root enclosure is inclusion-isotone on
nonnegative intervals. Each finite ball operation in
[[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] contains the exact ball
image. A `split-domain`, `entire`, `domain-error`, `overflow`, or
`inconclusive` status makes no finite claim. For a finite expression DAG
whose operation nodes all return finite enclosures, every exact node value
from every admissible input assignment belongs to its computed node
enclosure; in particular, the root enclosure contains the exact range. If any
node returns a non-finite status, no finite DAG enclosur”. Consumer use: The declared direct dependency thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound supports this item’s specification and proof..
